name: Carlos Nakamura

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I’m with the independent Work Futures Panel. We have no ties to employers, AI companies, unions, parties or government, and we sell nothing. Your answers are confidential. What does a normal day at work look like?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I am 43 and an experienced developer on course-booking software for a tech company, with a bachelor’s degree. I use AI every day for a first pass, then test the calendar myself; I know the system well, but I am not the quickest engineer. My wife Leena translates freelance, and our two school-age children and mortgage leave us with less than one month saved, so I watch her invoices as closely as my own pay.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau. Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d tell my team an AI helper can write routine calendar checks, but a learner still needs the right class at the right time. I use AI every day for first drafts and then test the booking with a real timetable.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I have a bachelor’s degree and have maintained this course-booking system for years, but the pay is low for software work. My wife Leena translates freelance, and with two children, a mortgage and less than one month saved, a quiet AI story still leaves us watching every invoice.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d keep fixing class-time clashes and ask support which enrolment errors caused the longest calls. We would stop the monthly meal kit and keep 45 for the mortgage account while my pay and Leena’s client work continue.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d feel anxious about money, though not about a small software change. A freelance invoice can arrive late whether AI is clever or not.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What clash sent you back to the code?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Two learners were booked into the same live lesson while the tutor had a different room. I found that a cancelled class had left one old seat in the calendar.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Does Leena share the bill worry?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: She keeps a list of translation clients and payment dates on the fridge. If one invoice is late, we shift grocery money and hope the mortgage still clears.

say: I tell colleagues **calendar checks** help only if learners reach the right class.
I test **AI drafts** against a real timetable before release.
think: I earn **below usual software pay** despite years on this system.
I worry **late translation invoices** and thin savings leave our mortgage exposed.
do: **Keep fixing** class-time clashes and ask support for long-call errors.
**Cancel the meal kit** and reserve 45 for mortgage payments while both incomes continue.
feel: **Anxious** about freelance timing and a thin cash buffer.
S0.quote: A freelance invoice can arrive late whether AI is clever or not.
fieldNote: His baseline worry is **uneven translation income** plus low developer pay, not only AI.
Daily AI drafts are checked against **real timetables** and support calls.

steps.text: Keep fixing course-calendar clashes and review support complaints
Cancel the monthly meal kit and reserve 45 for mortgage payments

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption. Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d say software that writes, books and answers customers will change both our course platform and Leena’s translation work. I would ask our manager for the number of junior and mid-level roles left after the routine tickets go.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I expect my own code hours to shrink, and I expect some of Leena’s clients to buy AI translations instead. We have less than one month saved, so cuts in both incomes would threaten the mortgage.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This month I’d learn a new AI check for timetable collisions using fake course records and compare it with three old mistakes. In the first year I’d ask management for a written staffing plan and look at paid classroom-technology support openings only if my hours fall and posts exist.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d be alarmed because it reaches both earnings at once. I like new tools, but I cannot ask the lender to accept an AI demonstration instead of money.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you tell Leena?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d say we should each list which paid tasks clients still ask us to do. If her translation orders drop, we would cut the weekend restaurant meal before taking money from the school account.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Why classroom support?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I have helped set up tutors’ tablets when our software failed, but I am not a field technician. I would apply only to paid openings that cover our mortgage share and basic bills.

say: I say **booking and translation** tasks could change together under AI.
I want a **written staffing count** for our course platform.
think: I expect **developer hours** and some of Leena’s translation orders to shrink.
I know **under one month saved** makes even two small cuts dangerous.
do: **Learn AI collision checks** on fake course records and three old errors.
**Request staffing plan** from management this year.
**Look for classroom support** only if hours fall and paid bill-covering posts exist.
feel: **Alarmed** because both household earnings could shrink.
S1.quote: I cannot ask the lender to accept an AI demonstration instead of money.
fieldNote: He actively learns a **new AI check**, yet worries both thinking-work incomes.
His **classroom support** option requires actual paid posts and wages that cover household bills.

steps.text: Learn AI timetable-collision checks using fake records and three old errors
Look for paid classroom-technology posts if hours fall and pay covers bills

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028. Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d say full AGI by 2028 could do most of my coding and Leena’s translation for less. Robots that set up classrooms may follow around 2031, but both our thinking-work incomes face the 2028 date.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I expect my developer job could go, and Leena’s clients could cut their orders at the same time. Less than one month saved would not cover the mortgage long enough for two people to hunt for work.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d ask the company for a written job date now, and Leena and I would list the mortgage, food and school payments due next month. If AGI arrives in 2028 and I am cut, I’d apply for paid on-site classroom support only if openings exist and pay covers our bills; if both incomes stop, we’d ask Leena’s mother for school pickup help during interviews.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d be alarmed and restless. I can make calls, but I cannot pretend an on-site role lasts beyond the later robots.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you say to the children?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d say both adults may need to look for work, and school still comes first. I would not promise the holiday we had discussed until we know the next pay cheque.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you take an unpaid support trial?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: No. I could help on a paid shift if one exists, but unpaid time takes away the hours I need to find wages.

say: I tell coworkers **thinking AGI by 2028** reaches our code and translation work.
I know **classroom robots around 2031** could later reach physical setup.
think: I expect **both incomes** could fall together in 2028.
I know **thin savings** cannot carry two job searches and the mortgage.
do: **List next bills**, ask for a written job date and postpone the holiday until pay is clear.
**Apply for classroom support** only if displaced after 2028 and paid offers cover bills.
**Ask Leena’s mother** for school pickups only if both adults interview at once.
feel: **Alarmed and restless** about two simultaneous income losses.
S2.quote: Less than one month saved would not cover the mortgage long enough for two people to hunt for work.
fieldNote: The **2028 thinking shock** reaches both software and translation before classroom robots arrive.
Family **pickup help** is conditional on simultaneous interviews, not a permanent childcare plan.

steps.text: Apply for paid classroom-support vacancies if displaced after 2028 and pay covers bills
Ask Leena’s mother for pickups only if both adults have interviews
Postpone the family holiday until the next pay cheque is clear

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031. Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d say five years before full AGI in 2031 should be used to learn which classroom problems still need a person. Robots for hands-on setup may arrive around 2034, so I will not sell hardware support as a permanent answer.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I could strengthen my practical network skills while still employed, but AI could also guide much of that work. Leena and I need to build cash before 2031, because our two thinking-work incomes may change together.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d buy a used practice router for 35 only if the mortgage and food are covered that month, then spend two evenings a month setting up a safe home network. We would save 75 monthly if both incomes arrive; if my developer job ends after 2031, I’d seek paid classroom equipment roles only where vacancies remain and pay covers our bills.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d be anxious, but five years gives me a task I can actually test. I cannot pay for a long course while the savings jar is nearly empty.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you practise?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d connect a spare tablet, break the connection on purpose and find the fault without touching a child’s account. If I cannot explain the repair to Leena in plain words, I would practise again.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if the router costs more than 35?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would leave it in the shop and use a free practice guide for now. The mortgage cannot be short because I wanted a training gadget.

say: I want **classroom problems** studied before AGI reaches our code in 2031.
I know **setup robots around 2034** could limit hardware support later.
think: I could learn **home network faults** while still employed.
I need **cash before 2031** because both household incomes face thinking AI.
do: **Buy a used router** only for 35 if mortgage and food are covered that month.
**Practise network setup** twice monthly; separately save 75 if both incomes arrive.
**Seek paid equipment work** only if displaced after 2031 and vacancies cover bills.
feel: **Anxious but purposeful** with a small affordable skills test.
S3.quote: The mortgage cannot be short because I wanted a training gadget.
fieldNote: His **35 router** turns adaptability into hands-on practice with a strict household budget gate.
The **75 saving** is independent of the router purchase and requires both incomes.

steps.text: Practise home-network faults with a 35 router only if mortgage and food are covered
Save 75 monthly when both household incomes arrive
Seek paid classroom-equipment vacancies if displaced after 2031 and pay covers bills

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036. Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d say ten years before full AGI in 2036 gives us time to compare real wages in different towns, not just job titles. Robots for classroom hardware may follow around 2039, after software and translation change.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Our children will be older, but I still expect a mortgage balance. If both incomes hold, we could save three months of bills and decide whether a move toward a larger job market would actually help.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d keep maintaining the booking system and update my work samples using fake course data every six months. Leena and I would save 90 monthly if both incomes hold, then compare written paid support offers in a larger town with housing and school costs; we would move only after an offer covers the move and our bills, and if my developer role ends after 2036 I would seek paid classroom-support vacancies there only where they remain.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d feel anxious about the money today, though less trapped by a far deadline. I want the children’s school and our mortgage in the arithmetic, not just a higher salary on paper.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you sell the house first?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: No; we would need a written offer and a clear housing plan before listing it. I would not put the children in limbo for a job advert.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would make a town too costly?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A salary that rises while rent, school travel and moving costs rise faster. I would write the monthly total beside our current mortgage before deciding.

say: I want **written wages and housing** compared before any move.
I know **robots around 2039** follow the earlier thinking-work change.
think: I may still have a **mortgage balance** in 2036.
I could save **three months of bills** if both incomes continue.
do: **Keep maintaining bookings** and update fake-data work samples twice yearly.
**Save 90 monthly** if both incomes hold; compare written offers with housing and school costs.
**Move for written offer** covering housing, school, moving costs and bills; seek paid support if displaced after 2036 and vacancies remain.
feel: **Anxious about current money**, though a long deadline leaves planning room.
S4.quote: I want the children’s school and our mortgage in the arithmetic, not just a higher salary on paper.
fieldNote: He makes a possible **move conditional** on written wages, housing and school costs.
His **fake-data samples** preserve a work record without exposing learner details, which he could show a hiring manager later.

steps.text: Keep maintaining the course-booking system and refresh fake-data work samples
Save 90 monthly while both household incomes continue
Move only for written offer covering housing, school, moving costs and bills
Seek paid classroom-support vacancies after 2036 only if displaced and wages cover bills

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 worries me most because it could hit my coding and Leena’s translation in the same year. Written job dates, real paid classroom-support vacancies that cover bills, and pickup help from Leena’s mother during overlapping interviews would help.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn’t ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: You did not ask whether we would move for work. We would consider relocating, but not for an online advert. A move would need a written bill-covering offer and a clear school plan.

headlineQuote: A move would need a written bill-covering offer and a clear school plan.
portrait: Carlos is a **43-year-old experienced developer** with a bachelor’s degree, lower pay and under one month saved.
He and Leena support **two school-age children** and a mortgage on software pay and freelance translation income.
He uses **AI daily**, checking generated code against real course timetables.
Both **thinking-work incomes** are exposed to AI, making Steady Disruption and fast AGI painful.
He tests **home networking** cheaply and considers moving only after comparing paid offers with school and housing costs.
biggestWorry: **AGI by 2028** could cut both software and translation income before the mortgage has a buffer.
whatWouldHelp: **Written dates**, bill-covering paid vacancies and conditional family pickup help would support simultaneous job searches.
